plan.summary: This 1-4 block fits an off-camp 12-week boxing plan with endurance as the main emphasis while keeping enough strength and power work to support punching, posture, and resilience. Week 1 establishes training baselines with simple rep-max assessments on the main lifts, one test lift per session, and the main training starts in Week 2. Because sparring is a priority and equipment is minimal, the lifting stays simple, safe, and low in total volume while conditioning does most of the work.

phaseOverview.label: Building
phaseOverview.focus: Build an aerobic base and repeat-effort capacity while establishing simple strength baselines and keeping power work crisp.

phaseOverview.label: Intensifying
phaseOverview.focus: Progress conditioning density and maintain basic strength with low-fatigue power and trunk work.

phaseOverview.label: Expressing
phaseOverview.focus: Keep endurance specific and sharp while preserving enough force and speed to support boxing work.

exercises.name: 1a. Countermovement Jump
exercises.notes: Land softly and reset between reps. Jump fast, not tired.

substitutionOptions.name: Box Jump
substitutionOptions.notes: Use a low box and stick the landing clean.

exercises.name: 2. Goblet Squat
exercises.notes: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Keep your torso tall and stop before form breaks. This establishes your baseline for future loading.

strengthAssessment.prompt: Warm up progressively, then work up to your heaviest clean set of 3-5 reps. Log the load and reps so the app can estimate your baseline.

performanceTarget.prompt: Beat the best clean top set over time without losing depth or position.

substitutionOptions.name: Double Dumbbell Front Squat
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if the goblet hold limits loading before the legs do.

exercises.name: 3. One-Arm Dumbbell Row
exercises.notes: Brace hard and pull the elbow toward the hip. Use a load you can control cleanly.

substitutionOptions.name: Chest-Supported Dumbbell Row
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if you want more support and less low-back demand.

exercises.name: 4. Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
exercises.notes: Push the hips back and keep the dumbbells close to the legs. Stop when hamstring tension is high and your back stays flat.

substitutionOptions.name: Single-Leg Dumbbell Romanian Deadlift
substitutionOptions.notes: Use this if available load is light and balance is solid.

exercises.name: 5. Front Plank
exercises.notes: Squeeze glutes, ribs down, and breathe behind the brace.

exercises.name: 6. Brisk Walk or Easy Jog
exercises.notes: Keep this relaxed and conversational. It should help recovery, not add fatigue.
